questions.question: How do you introduce yourself in an interview?
questions.title: Self Introduction
questions.direct_answer: A good intro is 60-90 seconds: who you are, what you know, one project you're proud of, and why this role. Structure: Present (who you are / recent) -> Past (what you've built / studied) -> Future (why this role). Be specific ('a Rails URL shortener with Sidekiq'), not generic ('I'm passionate about coding'); end on why THIS company/role excites you. Practice it out loud so it's natural, not memorized. The intro sets the tone and gives the interviewer hooks to ask follow-ups, so plant the things you want to be asked about.

interviewer_intent.testing: Whether you have a 60-90s intro (Present/Past/Future) that's specific and ends on why this role.
interviewer_intent.common_mistake: A generic 'passionate about coding' intro, or rambling past 2 minutes with no structure.
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: 60-90s: Present (who you are) -> Past (what you've built) -> Future (why this role). Be specific; end on why THIS role; practice out loud.

sections.title: Intro Flow
sections.content:
Present -> Past -> Future, specific, ~75 seconds.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  P[Present: who you are] --> Pa[Past: what you've built]
  Pa --> F[Future: why this role]
```

sections.title: A sample intro
sections.content:
```ruby
# Sample 75-second intro:

# Present: 'I'm a recent CS grad; I've spent the last year building Rails apps
#          and contributing to a couple of open-source gems.'
# Past:   'My main project is a URL shortener in Rails 7 with Sidekiq workers
#          and a Redis cache — I learned a lot about N+1 queries and background jobs.'
# Future: 'I'm excited about this role because you all use Rails at scale,
#          and I want to grow into a backend engineer who ships reliably.'

# Avoid: 'I'm passionate about coding and love learning new technologies.'
```

sections.title: Common Mistakes
items: A generic 'passionate about coding' intro — be specific about a project.
Rambling past 2 minutes with no structure — keep it 60-90s.
Not ending on why THIS role — the interviewer wants to hear the fit.

sections.title: Key Takeaways
items: A good intro is 60-90 seconds: who you are, what you know, one project, why this role.
Structure: Present (who you are) -> Past (what you've built) -> Future (why this role).
Be specific ('a Rails URL shortener with Sidekiq'), not generic ('passionate about coding').
End on why THIS company/role excites you.
Practice out loud so it's natural, not memorized; plant hooks for follow-ups.
